options.text: Using as many resources as possible to grow the economy
Meeting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs
Stopping all industrial development
Only using resources that are found underground

questions.explanation: Sustainable development means meeting current needs while ensuring that future generations can also meet their needs. It involves balancing economic growth with environmental protection and resource conservation.

questions.stem: What is the difference between finite and renewable resources?

options.text: Finite resources are cheaper; renewable resources are expensive
Finite resources will eventually run out; renewable resources can be replenished
Finite resources are found in the sea; renewable resources are found on land
There is no difference

questions.explanation: Finite resources (like fossil fuels and metal ores) exist in limited amounts and will eventually run out. Renewable resources (like timber, wind, and solar energy) can be replenished naturally or through management.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a finite resource?

options.text: Timber from managed forests
Wind energy
Crude oil
Solar energy

questions.explanation: Crude oil is a finite resource because it takes millions of years to form and is being used much faster than it can be replaced. Once it runs out, it cannot be replenished on a human timescale.

questions.stem: How does recycling contribute to sustainability?

options.text: It creates more waste
It reduces the use of finite raw materials, saves energy, and decreases the amount of waste sent to landfill
It only benefits companies financially
It increases pollution levels

questions.explanation: Recycling conserves finite raw materials, requires less energy than extracting new resources, and reduces the volume of waste going to landfill. All of these factors support sustainability.

questions.stem: Why is it important for the chemical industry to develop sustainable practices?

options.text: Only to reduce costs
To reduce environmental impact, conserve resources, and ensure raw materials remain available for the future
Because the government forces them to
It is not important for the chemical industry

questions.explanation: The chemical industry relies heavily on finite resources and can produce significant pollution. Sustainable practices help protect the environment, conserve resources, and ensure the long-term viability of the industry.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a sustainable practice?

options.text: Extracting as many minerals as possible from mines
Using renewable energy sources and recycling waste products
Dumping chemical waste in rivers
Cutting down forests without replanting

questions.explanation: Using renewable energy and recycling waste products are sustainable practices because they reduce dependence on finite resources and minimise environmental damage.

questions.stem: What does 'life cycle assessment' help determine about a product?

options.text: Only how long the product lasts
The total environmental impact at every stage, from raw material extraction to disposal
Only how much the product costs
Only how the product is manufactured

questions.explanation: A life cycle assessment (LCA) evaluates the environmental impact at every stage of a product's life: raw material extraction, manufacturing, transport, use, and disposal or recycling. This helps identify where improvements can be made.
